United Nations secretary-general candidate Rebeca Grynspan speaks during the UN Town Hall at the United Nations headquarters in New York City on July 23, 2026 [Eduardo Munoz/Reuters]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 28 Nov 202628 Nov 2026
More than 400 people have signed an open letter urging Costa Rica’s candidate to lead the United Nations, Rebeca Grynspan, to speak out after her government denied entry to UN special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territory Francesca Albanese.
In an open letter published by the Costa Rican news outlet SURCOS Digital on Friday, signatories urged UN secretary-general frontrunner Grynspan to press Costa Rica to admit Albanese, who is being held for a second night at an airport near San Jose.

The signatories asked Grynspan to implore the Costa Rican government to “reconsider its decision, allow Francesca Albanese to enter the country and guarantee her rights to freedom of expression”.
“We believe that the independence of someone aspiring to hold the position of Secretary General is also expressed in their ability to defend the principles of the Organization when these are compromised by actions of the very State that promotes their candidacy,” said the letter, spearheaded by Juliana Martinez Franzoni, a professor at the University of Costa Rica.
UN human rights chief Volker Turk has already urged Costa Rica to reconsider.
Grynspan did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

An Indian soldier stands guard on an armoured vehicle, near the site of a gun battle in Zanglapora, about 65km (40 miles) south of Srinagar, in Indian-administered Kashmir, Wednesday, November 18, 2026 [Dar Yasin/AP Photo]By Muheet Ul IslamPublished On 28 Nov 202628 Nov 2026
Kulgam and Srinagar, Indian-administered Kashmir – After a seven-day search, Indian security forces trapped Mohammad Lateef Bhat in a mosque in Zangalpora village, in Indian-administered Kashmir’s Kulgam district.
A gunfight broke out and Bhat was killed on November 18. Described as a commander of the Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT), a Pakistan-based armed group, Bhat was accused of having shot at soldiers of India’s Central Reserve Police Force a week earlier with another fighter. Three soldiers were injured. His associate was also killed in the days after that attack.
But it was Bhat’s death that grabbed national headlines.
Indian Home Minister Amit Shah, the country’s second-most powerful person after Prime Minister Narendra Modi, told a public gathering that Bhat had been the last local armed fighter before he was killed.
“This development marks a significant change in the security situation in the [Kashmir] valley. It is a matter of pride for us,” Shah said. “No Kashmiri youth is currently involved in terrorist activities in the valley.”
Jammu and Kashmir police also claimed that it was the first time since the armed rebellion against Indian rule in Kashmir began in 1989 that the LeT had no local fighters.
But analysts and former security officials say the armed conflict has not gone away but merely changed form.

A member of the Palestinian Civil Defence douses the flames on a car targeted in an Israeli strike in Gaza City on November 23, 2026 [Omar Al Qattaa/AFP]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 28 Nov 202628 Nov 2026
Two staff members of Doctors Without Borders, the humanitarian relief agency known by its French initials MSF, have been killed in an Israeli strike on one of its clinics in Gaza City.
“We are devastated and outraged by the killing of two of our colleagues, both watchmen, in an Israeli strike on one of our Gaza clinics tonight,” MSF said on X on Friday.

It called the attack a “direct hit” and said the deaths bring the number of its staff killed in Gaza to 17.
The agency’s premises were “clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military”, the group said.
It called for those responsible to be held accountable.
In a statement following the strike, the Israeli military claimed, without providing evidence, that the two workers were members of Hamas.
World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called the attack “outrageous and unacceptable”.
“Those risking their lives to save others must be protected, not attacked,” he wrote on X.
The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor condemned the “attack on a clearly marked MSF clinic” and accused Israel of “systematic targeting of humanitarian personnel and facilities”.

Heavy rain and flooding have begun to ease along the US East Coast as power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of holiday storms.
The storms disrupted travel and downed trees and power lines, leading to water rescues in multiple states, from New York to Virginia.

In New York City, preparations were under way for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after an unprecedented postponement because of rain and high winds.
The parade, an annual spectacle usually held on Thanksgiving Day, sees brightly coloured balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan. The festivities also kick off the holiday shopping season for the US.
The same balloons and floats, and most of the original celebrities, are still set to take part, organisers said.
Elsewhere, wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain moved across northern New England. Cold rain was reported in parts of the Midwest, including the Ohio Valley and the lower Great Lakes.
While conditions are expected to improve across the entire eastern US, the National Weather Service warned that “this huge system will take some time to weaken”.

The abduction of Tanzanian opposition activist Twaha Salim Mwaipaya in Kenya has renewed concerns over the safety of government critics fleeing political repression [File: Ben Curtis/AP Photo]By Vivianne WanderaPublished On 28 Nov 202628 Nov 2026
Nairobi, Kenya – On October 25, 2026, Tanzanian opposition activist Twaha Salim Mwaipaya was travelling in a taxi to visit friends in Kamulu, in Kenya’s Machakos County, when three vehicles intercepted it.
According to the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR), unidentified individuals forcibly removed him from the taxi and took him away. His whereabouts remain unknown.
Amnesty International reported that the vehicles included a Toyota Land Cruiser Hardtop. The organisation called on Kenyan authorities to establish Mwaipaya’s whereabouts, guarantee his safety and investigate the circumstances of his disappearance.
The International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) and the World Organisation Against Torture (OMCT) subsequently described the incident as an enforced disappearance and called for an independent investigation, including into possible cross-border involvement.
The identities of those responsible have not been established, and it remains unclear who ordered the abduction.
Mwaipaya, a former youth organiser of Tanzania’s opposition party Chadema, had fled to Kenya in 2025, citing threats to his safety.
On November 3, Kenya’s inspector general of police, Douglas Kanja, appeared before the High Court to explain the activist’s whereabouts. He denied that Kenyan police had arrested or detained Mwaipaya.
“We do not have him in our custody,” Kanja told the court, adding that investigations were ongoing. He acknowledged that Mwaipaya’s relatives had reported him missing at a police station ...

A father carrying his young daughter casts his ballot beside ballot boxes for city councillors and borough chiefs at a polling station on November 28, 2026, in Taipei, Taiwan [Cheng Chia Huang/Getty Images]By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP, AP and ReutersPublished On 28 Nov 202628 Nov 2026
Taiwan is choosing mayors, council members and other local leaders across its 22 cities and counties in an election that has been unusually competitive in some of the island’s biggest cities.
Polls opened at 8am (00:00 GMT) on Saturday and will close at 4pm (08:00 GMT), with results expected early in the evening.

Voters are casting ballots at schools, temples and community centres.
About 11,000 positions are at stake in the “nine-in-one” elections, named for the nine categories of local government posts being contested.
Taipei mayoral race
A key contest is for the mayor of the capital, Taipei, a traditional stronghold of the opposition Kuomintang (KMT).
Mayor Chiang Wan-an of the KMT, who won by a double-digit margin in the last election and is seen as a possible future presidential candidate, faces a strong challenge from Puma Shen of the governing Democratic Progressive Party (DPP).
Shen is an academic-turned-lawmaker and an expert on China’s information warfare. China has denounced him, and Chinese police say he is wanted for “separatism”. Demonstrators march during a protest over high electricity rates, the surging cost of living and deteriorating basic services in San Juan, Puerto Rico, on November 27, 2026 [Alejandro Granadillo/AP]By Al Jazeera Staff, AP and ReutersPublished On 28 Nov 202628 Nov 2026
Thousands of Puerto Ricans have protested in the capital, San Juan, as anger and frustration erupted over record-high electricity rates, the surging cost of living, deteriorating basic services and other issues.
Retirees, university students, bus drivers and others joined Friday’s protest organised by some 30 groups ranging from unions to religious organisations. The crowds gathered in front of a mall for what organisers dubbed the “Day of National Outrage”.

Hundreds of demonstrators arrived by bus in San Juan from dozens of cities and towns across the island.
Asked what problems Puerto Rico had, 74-year-old Radames Garcia Badillo said: “Where to start? The outrage is absolute.”
He said that power and water services are unreliable and that his neighbourhood goes dark at least once a week for several hours. He also decried a sharp increase in the cost of living.
“We’re buying less because things are extremely expensive,” he said. “For us retirees, it is essential to make every dollar stretch.”
The protest, one of the largest in the US territory since Governor Jenniffer Gonzalez took office in January 2025, grew throughout the day as demonstrators took over one of the island’s main highways, forcing its closure.
